# Operation Steel Opera — Special Instructions

 · DRAFT — MISSION-MAKER REVIEW
operation-steel-opera-spins · Revision draft-4
Persian Gulf · Scenario start 1 June 2018, 06:00

<a id="position-content-0"></a>

## 1 Applicability and mission basis

<a id="position-content-0-0"></a>

**1.1** **Status.** This is a mission-derived SPINS draft for Operation Steel Opera. Mission configuration is stated as configured, not as a live service guarantee. Paragraphs marked “Draft procedure” propose coordination rules for adoption by the mission maker.


<a id="position-content-0-1"></a>

**1.2** **Applicability.** These standing instructions apply to runs of the exact source mission identified in the references. They remain a complete baseline until revised; no ATO-period amendment or expiry has been invented.


<a id="position-content-0-2"></a>

**1.3** **Scenario clock.** The mission starts on 1 June 2018 at 06:00 on its scenario clock. A UTC offset and end-of-mission time are not established in the archive. Use the same explicitly briefed clock for all launch, entry, support, and recovery times.


<a id="position-content-0-3"></a>

**1.4** **Mission tasking.** The source contains no authored Player or Client aircraft and no blue tasking paragraph. Flight callsigns, target assignments, expected standard conventional loads (SCLs), routes, fuel states, and recovery assignments are not supplied. Issue these in flight tasking; a map target label or AI loadout is not a player assignment.


<a id="position-content-0-4"></a>

**1.5** **Draft procedure — flight brief.** Before launch, each flight lead shall identify the assigned task, aircraft and SCL, departure and recovery location, alternate, radio plan, fuel limits, planned control-area crossings, and abort conditions. Resolve the open items in the mission-maker annex before using the document as an issued order.


<a id="position-content-0-5"></a>

**1.6** **Weather snapshot.** The configured temperature is 40 °C, visibility is 80 km, and cloud-base value is 4,200 m with Preset1. Fog and dust are disabled. Obtain the current in-simulator altimeter setting, runway, wind, and recovery condition; these instructions do not assign a carrier recovery case.



<a id="position-content-1"></a>

## 2 Communications, navigation aids, and support

<a id="position-content-1-0"></a>

**2.1** **Frequency basis.** Carrier and template data below come from the mission. Airfield VHF channels come from the installed Persian Gulf terrain database. A frequency entry does not establish that a human controller is staffed or that an inactive aircraft has launched.


<a id="node-service-plan"></a>

| Agency / platform | Radio | Navigation aids | Status / use |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| CVN-75 Harry S. Truman | 127.500 MHz AM | TACAN 75X, ident KU; ICLS 5 | Programmed on the carrier. The briefing instead lists TACAN 4X. Resolve this discrepancy before recovery. |
| ARCO (briefing entry) | 210.000 MHz AM | TACAN 11Y | Briefing only. No matching active ARCO service is established by the archive. |
| E-2C template / MAGIC 1-1 | 251.000 MHz; AM mode value | No dedicated TACAN recorded | Late activation. No activation action for this group was found in the inspected mission. |
| S-3B tanker template / TEXACO 1-1 | 251.000 MHz; AM mode value | TACAN 1X, ident TKR in template task | Late activation; does not match the ARCO briefing entry. Not a guaranteed refueling service. |

<a id="position-content-1-2"></a>

**2.2** **Draft procedure — initial contact.** Identify callsign, number and type of aircraft, position, altitude with reference, intended activity, and requested clearance. Read back the assigned route, altitude, clearance limit, and reporting requirement. Use the actual assigned agency and channel; do not treat the table’s inactive templates as available controllers.


<a id="position-content-1-3"></a>

**2.3** **Draft procedure — support availability.** Confirm tanker identity, channel, beacon, station, operating altitude, and availability before relying on aerial refueling. A fuel plan shall remain viable if the unverified support listed above is unavailable.


<a id="position-content-1-4"></a>

**2.4** **Draft procedure — navigation check.** For carrier recovery, reconcile the programmed and briefing-listed aids in [Table 1](#node-service-plan) before launch. Verify beacon identification and establish communications before committing to the recovery.



<a id="position-content-2"></a>

## 3 Airspace control and restrictions

<a id="position-content-2-0"></a>

**3.1** **Control-measure names.** Use the exact mission drawing names in clearances and reports. The mission contains named civil control volumes and a military-route label; its civil-traffic script gives these volumes population-specific behavior. Do not treat every drawn polygon or hidden trigger zone as a general aircraft exclusion area.


<a id="node-control-volumes"></a>

| Measure | Recorded vertical definition | Scope / qualification |

| OMDB CTR-W | 10,000–28,000 ft MSL in traffic configuration | Drawing reads FL280–10000. Applies to generated civil traffic crossing the polygon. |
| OMDB CTA | Ground–12,000 ft MSL | Dubai terminal area; overlaps must not be assumed to be empty. |
| OMAA CTR | 10,000–28,000 ft MSL | Abu Dhabi civil traffic volume. Drawing reads FL280–10000. |
| OMAA\_APP | 4,000–10,000 ft MSL | Abu Dhabi approach volume. |

| OMRK CTA | Ground–6,500 ft MSL | Traffic-script restriction is filtered to Ras Al Khaimah traffic. |
| OMFJ CTA | Ground–7,500 ft MSL | Traffic-script restriction is filtered to Fujairah traffic. |
| MRR1 | Map label: FL180–UNLTD; civil script: ground–17,000 ft MSL | Different populations use different vertical definitions. No military level allocation by direction is supplied. |
| CVN75\_CATCC | Civil-traffic exclusion at all altitudes; 5 NM planning buffer | Fixed rectangular drawing. The source does not assign a military entry altitude or moving carrier-control volume. |

<a id="node-civil-vertical-separation"></a>

### 3.2 Vertical separation from civil traffic

<a id="position-content-2-2-0"></a>

**3.2.1** **Draft rule — remain above or below.** Military flights shall remain outside the vertical limits of the civil traffic volumes unless a crossing has been specifically coordinated. Select an altitude below the civil floor or above the civil ceiling, while respecting the assigned route altitude and terrain clearance. A route drawn through the horizontal footprint does not by itself permit flight within the civil altitude band.


<a id="position-content-2-2-1"></a>

**3.2.2** **Draft planning margin.** For this SPINS, plan at least 1,000 ft below a raised civil floor or above a civil ceiling. This margin is a proposed mission rule. The table uses feet MSL from the traffic configuration. It provides planning limits, not a terrain-clearance guarantee or permission to enter another overlapping volume.


<a id="node-civil-vertical-limits"></a>

**Table 3. Draft military under/over limits — all numeric altitudes in feet MSL**

| Civil volume | Configured civil band | Underflight limit | Overflight limit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| OMDB CTR-E | 10,000–28,000 | At or below 9,000 | At or above 29,000 |
| OMDB CTR-W | 10,000–28,000 | At or below 9,000 | At or above 29,000 |
| OMDB CTA | Ground–12,000 | No underflight option | At or above 13,000 |
| OMRK CTA | Ground–6,500 | No underflight option | At or above 7,500 |
| OMAA CTR | 10,000–28,000 | At or below 9,000 | At or above 29,000 |
| OMAA\_APP | 4,000–10,000 | At or below 3,000 | At or above 11,000 |
| OMAA CTA | Ground–10,000 | No underflight option | At or above 11,000 |
| MRR1 | Ground–17,000 | No underflight option | At or above 18,000 |
| OMFJ CTA | Ground–7,500 | No underflight option | At or above 8,500 |

<a id="position-content-2-2-3"></a>

**3.2.3** **Ground-based areas.** There is no underflight option for a volume extending down to ground. Use its overflight limit or remain laterally outside it. This applies to OMDB CTA, OMAA CTA, OMRK CTA, OMFJ CTA, and the civil-traffic band in MRR1.


<a id="position-content-2-2-4"></a>

**3.2.4** **Overlapping areas.** Remain outside every applicable civil band with the planning margin. Being below one floor can place the aircraft inside another volume. For example, where OMAA\_APP (4,000–10,000) and OMAA CTR (10,000–28,000) overlap, the common outside options are at or below 3,000 or at or above 29,000 ft MSL, subject to route and terrain limits. If a ground-based CTA also occupies the lower option, remain above the combined ceiling or outside the overlap.


<a id="position-content-2-2-5"></a>

**3.2.5** **Climb and descent.** Complete the altitude change outside the affected lateral boundary. Do not descend from above a civil volume to below it, or climb from below to above, through occupied civil altitudes without coordinated crossing instructions. If terrain, route restrictions, or aircraft capability prevent an outside altitude, remain clear and obtain a revised route or clearance.


<a id="position-content-2-2-6"></a>

**3.2.6** **MRR1.** The mission places generated civil traffic at or below 17,000 ft MSL in MRR1 and labels the military route FL180–UNLTD. Maintain the assigned military level and at least 1,000 ft above the civil ceiling using a common altitude reference. FL180 is a pressure flight level; confirm the pressure-altitude relationship instead of treating it as exactly 18,000 ft MSL. Other overlapping civil volumes still require coordination.


<a id="position-content-2-2-7"></a>

**3.2.7** **Traffic outside the volumes.** The polygons constrain the configured generator, not every possible aircraft. Civil flights also use 30,000–40,000-ft entry/exit levels outside these areas. An overflight altitude clear of one volume does not establish an empty traffic area. Continue traffic checks and avoid using AI routing constraints as guaranteed separation.



<a id="position-content-2-3"></a>

**3.3** **Draft procedure — clearance to enter.** Before entering a civil terminal area, CVN75\_CATCC, or a crossing involving conflicting traffic, obtain coordination from the designated mission controller. State the measure name, entry point, intended track, altitude, and exit. Report entry and clear. If no controller or published flight deconfliction is available, remain clear until the conflict is resolved.


<a id="node-mrr-procedure"></a>

**3.4** **Draft procedure — MRR1.** Use the drawn MRR1 footprint and the military FL180–UNLTD label in [Table 2](#node-control-volumes). Assign a specific direction and flight level during the flight brief. The eastbound and westbound arrows do not themselves allocate odd/even levels or separation. Do not use the civil script’s 17,000-ft ceiling as a military route clearance.


<a id="position-content-2-5"></a>

**3.5** **Draft procedure — civil-area crossing.** Apply the underflight or overflight limits in [Section 3.2](#node-civil-vertical-separation) before crossing a civil footprint. Obtain specific coordination if the planned route requires passage through its civil band. Keep climbs, descents, and holds outside the volume until that coordination is complete.


<a id="position-content-2-6"></a>

**3.6** **CATCC geometry.** CVN75\_CATCC is a fixed rectangle measuring 185,000 by 92,500 m. The carrier starts outside it: the shortest mission-grid distance from the starting position to the rectangle is about 58.9 NM. It does not follow the ship. Carrier protection and aircraft entry procedures therefore require an explicit mission-maker decision.


<a id="node-control-schematic"></a>

![Two mission-grid diagrams show civil control polygons, MRR1, a shipping blockade, the CATCC rectangle, and the carrier starting position.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Figure 1. Control measures from the source mission. Fixed CATCC drawing and actual carrier start are shown separately.

<a id="position-content-2-8"></a>

**3.7** **Other map features.** DAISY, GATSBY, CARRAWAY, and JORDAN are area labels on the map. ADF-1 and ADF-2 are hidden trigger zones without published vertical limits or entry procedures. None of these names alone grants clearance, establishes a weapons-free area, or identifies an assigned target.

## 4 Airfield operations

<a id="position-content-3-0"></a>

**4.1** **Airfield coordination.** The mission contains drawn HI/LO entries for Al Dhafra, including a connection on the Al Minhad side. Its civil-traffic generator separately serves Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah, and Fujairah. Civil airports and their drawn routes are not automatically military departure, recovery, or alternate assignments.

<a id="position-content-3-2"></a>

**4.2** **Draft procedure — common departure and recovery.** Obtain the active runway and traffic information from local control. Confirm that the runway and departure path are clear before entering or departing. For arrival, report position, altitude, fuel state, intended recovery, and abnormal conditions. Coordinate any alternate or diversion; this SPINS does not assign one.


<a id="node-al-dhafra-entry-routes"></a>

### 4.3 Al Dhafra / OMAM — HI and LO entry routes

<a id="position-content-3-3-0"></a>

**4.3.1** **Procedure names.** Use the named arrivals below in flight briefs and on the radio. These are Operation Steel Opera mission procedures. Each title uses a name and revision number, such as OPERA ONE (OPERA1). The names identify the drawn routes; they do not create new navigation fixes. Procedure revision ONE is independent of paragraph numbering and this document’s draft revision.


<a id="node-al-dhafra-entry-table"></a>

| Arrival / identifier | Entry | Connection |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| OPERA ONE (OPERA1) | Northern HI | WEST ARC |
| MINHA ONE (MINHA1) | Al Minhad-side HI | SOUTH ARC / EAST TRANSITION |
| TENOR ONE (TENOR1) | Outer northeastern HI | NORTH JOIN to OPERA ONE, or EAST TRANSITION as assigned |
| LYRIC ONE (LYRIC1) | Northwestern LO | OPERA ONE / WEST ARC join; altitude transition requires coordination |

<a id="position-content-3-3-2"></a>

**4.3.2** **OPERA ONE arrival.** Use the northern HI entry and its drawn western-side route. The high-route annotation is UNLTD-12000. Continue toward WEST ARC, the nominal 15 DME arc west/northwest of MA, for the assigned airfield entry.


<a id="position-content-3-3-3"></a>

**4.3.3** **MINHA ONE arrival.** Use the HI route from the Al Minhad side. Its straight leg reaches MA and the drawing continues to the southern arc and eastern connection. The high-route annotation is UNLTD-12000. SOUTH ARC is the nominal 15 DME arc south/southeast of MA; use the assigned EAST TRANSITION and recovery clearance.


<a id="position-content-3-3-4"></a>

**4.3.4** **TENOR ONE arrival.** Use the outer northeastern HI entry, annotated UNLTD-12000. At the branching area, take NORTH JOIN toward OPERA ONE, or the eastern continuation when assigned. Include the selected transition in the entry clearance.


<a id="position-content-3-3-5"></a>

**4.3.5** **LYRIC ONE arrival.** Use the northwestern LO entry and its curved route toward OPERA ONE. The source annotation is 4000-8000. Coordinate the altitude change and the WEST ARC connection before joining the high-route structure.


<a id="position-content-3-3-6"></a>

**4.3.6** **Civil traffic — route-specific application.** Apply the vertical limits in [Section 3.2](#node-civil-vertical-separation) to the named arrival. The source geometry gives the following intersections; the route name and HI/LO label do not override the civil bands.


<a id="node-arrival-civil-separation"></a>

| Arrival / segment | Intersected civil volume | Draft vertical guidance |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| OPERA ONE | OMAA\_APP and OMAA CTR | Above OMAA\_APP: at or above 11,000 ft MSL. At the CTR crossing: at or below 9,000 or at or above 29,000. Retaining the HI band prevents assuming the lower option; resolve the descent/re-route before entry. Where both volumes overlap, apply the combined limits. |
| LYRIC ONE | OMAA CTR | The drawn 4,000–8,000 low band is below the 10,000-ft civil floor. Keep at or below 9,000 ft MSL and within the assigned low-route band until clear. Coordinate before climbing into the HI structure. |

Continue checking for traffic and any revised clearance. |

<a id="position-content-3-3-8"></a>

**4.3.7** **DME reference.** Distance Measuring Equipment (DME) indicates slant-range distance to the selected navigation aid, in nautical miles. Both arcs reference Al Dhafra MA VORTAC: 114.90 MHz / TACAN 96X. Identify MA and use its DME readout. The nominal instruction “15 DME MA” means an indicated distance of 15 NM from MA. [Reference 5](#citation-navigation-basis)


<a id="node-al-dhafra-dme-arcs"></a>

**Table 7. Al Dhafra DME-arc transitions**

| Transition | DME reference / nominal distance | Drawn sector and use |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| WEST ARC | MA / 96X — 15 DME | West to northwest of MA. Used by the western-side arrival connection. The arc excludes the straight spoke to the station and the curved join at its outer end. |
| SOUTH ARC | MA / 96X — 15 DME | South to southeast of MA, at the end of the Al Minhad-side route. Connects with the eastern-side layout. The straight route through MA is not part of the arc. |

<a id="position-content-3-3-10"></a>

**4.3.8** **Arc distance basis.** Both 15 DME values are nominal procedure distances reconstructed from the mission drawings. The main western arc vertices lie 14.84–14.95 NM horizontally from MA; the main southern arc lies 15.17–15.39 NM away. Joining turns bend inside those ranges. The figure preserves the drawn geometry and adds a 15-NM plan-view reference circle; cockpit DME also includes the height difference to the station.


<a id="position-content-3-3-11"></a>

**4.3.9** **Draft procedure — flying the arc.** Tune and identify MA, confirm the assigned arc and altitude, and maintain the nominal 15 DME indication while following the cleared direction. Confirm the arc exit and subsequent recovery instruction before turning onto the next leg. The drawn vertex order does not itself assign an inbound direction, magnetic radial, or runway.


<a id="position-content-3-3-12"></a>

**4.3.10** **Altitude bands.** The source annotates HI routes as UNLTD-12000, the LO route as 4000-8000, and the eastern/southeastern segment as 12000-4000. These correspond to a high band at 12,000 and above, a low band from 4,000 to 8,000, and a connecting band from 4,000 to 12,000. The text objects do not specify units or altitude datum. Confirm those conventions and the transition clearance in the flight brief; do not silently substitute flight levels for the drawn numbers.

<a id="node-tacan-only-guide"></a>

#### 4.3.11 TACAN-only cockpit guide

<a id="position-content-3-3-14-0"></a>

**4.3.11.1** **Equipment and setup.** Use MA on TACAN 96X in ground transmit/receive mode, with TACAN selected as the navigation source. Identify MA and confirm valid bearing and distance indications. Use the aircraft’s normal heading indicator, altimeter, and a plotted route/briefing card. These instructions assume no GPS or INS steering.


<a id="position-content-3-3-14-1"></a>

**4.3.11.2** **Radial versus bearing.** A radial is the magnetic direction FROM MA. The bearing-pointer head points TO MA; its reciprocal gives the FROM radial. For example, a bearing to MA of 175 degrees corresponds approximately to MA radial 355. Aircraft heading is a separate quantity. Read the radial and range together to locate the aircraft.


<a id="node-ma-tacan-checkpoints"></a>

**Table 8. Calculated MA planning checkpoints — magnetic FROM radials and horizontal map ranges**

| Checkpoint | MA radial (magnetic) | Map range (NM) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| OPERA ONE entry | 355° | 47.0 |
| MINHA ONE entry | 043° | 65.9 |
| TENOR ONE entry | 022° | 83.2 |
| LYRIC ONE entry | 320° | 58.4 |
| NORTH JOIN branching area | 007° | 35.6 |
| NORTH JOIN / OPERA ONE join | 352° | 30.5 |
| LYRIC ONE / OPERA ONE join | 305° | 21.7 |
| WEST ARC northwestern main-arc end | 295° | 14.9 |
| WEST ARC western main-arc end | 267° | 14.9 |
| SOUTH ARC southern main-arc end | 177° | 15.3 |
| SOUTH ARC southeastern main-arc end | 129° | 15.2 |

<a id="position-content-3-3-14-3"></a>

**4.3.11.3** **Checkpoint basis.** The radial references use the source vertices, a projection checked against 101 installed terrain beacon coordinates, and the installed DCS magnetic model for June 2018 (1.98 degrees east at MA). Values are rounded planning references. Main-arc endpoint entries locate the measured circular portions; joining turns extend beyond them. They are not assigned arc-entry or exit clearances.


<a id="position-content-3-3-14-4"></a>

**4.3.11.4** **Range interpretation.** The table gives horizontal map range; TACAN displays slant range. Compare both radial and distance and account for altitude above MA. A point 15 NM horizontally from MA reads about 15.1 DME at 12,000 ft above the aid and about 15.7 DME at 28,000 ft above it. For WEST ARC or SOUTH ARC, the instructed nominal 15 DME is the cockpit indication. DME-derived speed and time-to-station reflect closure to MA; do not treat them as actual groundspeed while flying around the arc.


<a id="position-content-3-3-14-5"></a>

**4.3.11.5** **Flying a radial leg.** For a cleared straight leg along a MA radial, set the appropriate inbound or outbound course and correct for wind while monitoring course deviation and DME trend. MINHA ONE’s initial straight leg is approximately MA radial 043 inbound toward MA; its reciprocal inbound course is approximately 223 degrees. Confirm the current indication and clearance before using those calculated values.


<a id="position-content-3-3-14-6"></a>

**4.3.11.6** **Flying the other route shapes.** OPERA ONE, TENOR ONE, and LYRIC ONE include legs that are not a single MA radial or constant-distance arc. Use the plotted fix-to-fix headings and successive radial/range checkpoints to check progress. Turning the bearing pointer toward MA would cut across those routes. If the brief does not provide a usable leg heading and next checkpoint, obtain heading instructions before entering the constrained segment.


<a id="position-content-3-3-14-7"></a>

**4.3.11.7** **Joining the 15 DME arc.** Approach on the cleared intercept leg and lead the turn so that the aircraft rolls out tangent to the arc near 15 DME. Set turn lead for groundspeed, bank, and wind. Do not use a fixed lead distance for every aircraft or begin an unplanned turn at the civil boundary.


<a id="position-content-3-3-14-8"></a>

**4.3.11.8** **Maintaining the arc.** For clockwise travel around MA, keep the station approximately abeam on the right; for counterclockwise travel, keep it approximately abeam on the left. Use small heading corrections and the DME trend: increasing range requires a correction toward MA, while decreasing range requires a correction away. Maintain the assigned altitude while monitoring the next FROM radial.


<a id="position-content-3-3-14-9"></a>

**4.3.11.9** **Leaving the arc.** Before reaching the cleared exit radial, identify the subsequent course or heading and lead the turn to capture it. Confirm the radial, DME, and subsequent course before leaving the arc. Maintain the assigned altitude until cleared for a change; an arc exit does not clear descent through civil airspace or establish a final approach.


<a id="position-content-3-3-14-10"></a>

**4.3.11.10** **Station passage and degraded indications.** Near or overhead MA, slant range need not reach zero and the bearing can change rapidly. Fly the briefed heading through station passage and confirm the outbound indication after it stabilizes. If identification, bearing, or range is lost, advise control, maintain the last safe assigned heading and altitude, and obtain revised instructions; do not enter another constrained segment on an unreliable fix.


<a id="position-content-3-3-14-11"></a>

**4.3.11.11** **Reporting example.** “OPERA ONE, MA radial three five five, four seven DME, \[assigned altitude\], request WEST ARC transition.” Report the actual cockpit DME and state the altitude reference. A radial/range fix establishes position; it does not provide traffic separation by itself.



<a id="position-content-3-3-15"></a>

**4.3.12** **Draft procedure — entry selection.** Brief the selected HI or LO branch using [Table 5](#node-al-dhafra-entry-table), the assigned altitude reference, and the intended transition to recovery. Contact Al Dhafra on 126.500 MHz AM with callsign, named arrival and transition, position, altitude, fuel state, and recovery intention. Example request: “Request OPERA ONE arrival, WEST ARC transition.” Obtain coordination before changing branch or altitude band.


<a id="position-content-3-3-16"></a>

**4.3.13** **Draft procedure — crossings and joins.** Remain on the briefed branch through the civil-airspace crossings. Coordinate the LO-to-HI join and any use of the eastern connecting band in advance. Nearby Abu Dhabi control-area limits and the civil arrival/departure flows still apply to their respective traffic; a military route line does not itself clear a crossing.


<a id="position-content-3-3-17"></a>

**4.3.14** **Draft procedure — recovery handover.** Obtain the runway, recovery sequence, and clearance from local control before leaving the entry route. An arrival name specifies the selected procedure; it does not by itself assign an altitude or landing clearance.



<a id="position-content-3-4"></a>

### 4.4 Al Minhad / OMDM

<a id="position-content-3-4-0"></a>

**4.4.1** **Mission definition.** The source defines a hidden circular Al Minhad trigger zone with a 3,000-m radius. The Al Minhad-side HI connection to Al Dhafra is shown in [Section 4.3](#node-al-dhafra-entry-routes). The zone itself does not define a circuit or instrument approach.


<a id="position-content-3-4-1"></a>

**4.4.2** **Draft procedure.** Brief the military departure and recovery before launch. Coordinate the route from Al Minhad with the Dubai and Sharjah civil flows. Join MRR1 only after the assigned direction, level, and crossing have been deconflicted.



<a id="position-content-3-5"></a>

### 4.5 Dubai International / OMDB

<a id="position-content-3-5-0"></a>

**4.5.1** **Published traffic paths.** Civil departures use OMDB\_SID1, OMDB\_SID2; arrivals use OMDB\_STAR. Configured arrival entry points are IVOBA, ASNIS, KUMBO. These are the mission’s named drawing paths, not certified instrument charts.


<a id="position-content-3-5-1"></a>

**4.5.2** **Traffic behavior.** Dubai departures are configured to appear airborne at 100 ft AGL and 170 KIAS; the configuration identifies runway 12R. Arrivals use a landing task. Expect runway-area traffic without a preceding taxi sequence.


<a id="position-content-3-5-2"></a>

**4.5.3** **Draft procedure.** Keep clear of the depicted arrival and departure paths unless the flight has an assigned crossing. Check the runway and final approach even when no aircraft has taxied. At fields with runway-overflight arrivals, maintain separation until the aircraft has passed clear; do not assume it will stop on the runway.

## 5 Carrier operations

<a id="position-content-4-0"></a>

**5.1** **Carrier group.** Carrier Strike Group 8 contains CVN-75 Harry S. Truman, CG-50 Valley Forge, DDG-96 Bainbridge, DDG-67 Cole, and DDG-107 Gravely. The carrier has a two-point route; it is not stationary. No cyclic launch/recovery schedule, final bearing, or recovery case is supplied.


<a id="position-content-4-1"></a>

**5.2** **Draft procedure — departure.** Obtain the assigned departure, initial altitude, radio transfer, and route to the operating area. Maintain awareness of the actual ship position and civil traffic. Do not use the distant fixed CATCC rectangle as a substitute for local carrier traffic instructions.


<a id="position-content-4-2"></a>

**5.3** **Draft procedure — recovery.** Call the carrier on the channel in [Table 1](#node-service-plan) and obtain current recovery instructions. Confirm the beacon discrepancy has been resolved, establish the assigned recovery case and sequence, and report fuel or system limitations before committing. No marshal radial, holding altitude, or emergency divert is invented here.


<a id="position-content-4-3"></a>

**5.4** **Plane guard and recovery tanker.** The SH-60B and S-3B exist as late-activation templates. The inspected triggers do not activate them. Treat rescue and recovery-tanker coverage as unavailable until specifically verified or added by the mission maker.



<a id="position-content-5"></a>

## 6 Civil air traffic and maritime restrictions

<a id="position-content-5-0"></a>

**6.1** **Civil traffic picture.** The embedded traffic generator is configured for up to 40 active aircraft, with a startup target of half that limit. It adds airport arrivals and departures, with entry and exit altitude selections of 30,000–40,000 ft. Actual numbers and flight paths depend on initialization, aircraft availability, traffic spacing, and AI behavior.


<a id="node-civil-gates"></a>

**Table 9. Civil traffic entry gates and shared exits**

| Airport flow | Arrival gates | Departure exits |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| DXB | IVOBA, ASNIS, KUMBO | LOTAV, REXOD, TOTOX, PARAR, RASKI, LUDID |
| AUH | IVOBA, HSA | LOTAV, REXOD, TOTOX, PARAR, RASKI, LUDID |
| SHJ | IVOBA, ASNIS, KUMBO | LOTAV, REXOD, TOTOX, PARAR, RASKI, LUDID |
| RKT | IVOBA, ASNIS, KUMBO | LOTAV, REXOD, TOTOX, PARAR, RASKI, LUDID |
| FJR | LUDID, RASKI, PARAR | LOTAV, REXOD, TOTOX, PARAR, RASKI, LUDID |

<a id="position-content-5-2"></a>

**6.2** **Draft procedure — unidentified traffic.** Do not classify a contact as hostile solely from its presence in an operating area, airline paint scheme, lack of response, or map label. Report identity uncertainty and keep clear while it is resolved. Flight tasking must supply the applicable engagement authority.


<a id="position-content-5-3"></a>

**6.3** **Shipping.** The shipping script is configured for up to 40 generated neutral vessels using the named port and sea-lane network. It applies a 0.5-NM lane offset and a 2-NM spawn-spacing criterion. These are generator parameters, not protected approach distances or weapons-release criteria.


<a id="position-content-5-4"></a>

**6.4** **BLOCKADE\_HORMUZ.** The mission defines a circular shipping blockade with a radius of 30,480 m (16.46 NM). The shipping generator adds a 0.5-NM buffer, plans to stop another 1 NM short, and seeks a holding position within its configured 5-NM holding radius. These are maritime-routing constraints; no airspace floor or ceiling is assigned.


<a id="position-content-5-5"></a>

**6.5** **Draft procedure — blockade and surface contacts.** Expect neutral traffic to hold outside the blockade rather than disappear. Do not interpret stopping, holding, or approaching a port as engagement authority. Coordinate any flight activity over the blockade with the mission controller and keep the maritime restriction separate from aircraft clearances.


<a id="position-content-5-6"></a>

**6.6** **Minerva Nike.** Minerva Nike is a blue-side merchant-vessel group with a unit-linked 3,000-m zone. The source does not publish a visit, boarding, attack, or rescue task for that vessel. Its presence and associated zone do not constitute player tasking.



<a id="position-content-6"></a>

## 7 Abnormal procedures and reporting

<a id="position-content-6-0"></a>

**7.1** **Draft procedure — lost communications.** Attempt the last assigned agency and channel, then the prebriefed alternate or relay. Avoid uncoordinated entry into occupied control areas. Use the flight’s published lost-communications route and recovery decision; if none exists, settle it during the flight brief before departure.


<a id="position-content-6-1"></a>

**7.2** **Draft procedure — fuel or aircraft emergency.** Advise the controlling agency of callsign, position, altitude, nature of the emergency, fuel/endurance, and intended action. Request priority and coordinate the recovery location. An unverified tanker is not an emergency-fuel plan.


<a id="position-content-6-2"></a>

**7.3** **Draft procedure — traffic conflict.** Maintain aircraft control, report the conflict, and coordinate the maneuver and subsequent clearance. The civil scripts do not provide a live controller or guarantee that AI aircraft remain within their planned altitude and lateral limits.


<div id="position-content-6-3"><p class="label">7.4</p>
<ol type="a" start="1">
<li>Entry/exit report: callsign, named measure, position, altitude, and next intention.
</li>
<li>Support request: callsign, requested service, position, fuel/endurance, and aircraft limitations.
</li>
<li>Mission completion: assigned task result, losses or damage, remaining stores and fuel, and recovery intention.
</li>
<li>Discrepancy report: observed condition, location/time, affected flight, and the specific instruction or aid involved.
</li>
</ol></div>



<a id="position-content-7"></a>

OPERA ONE has a CTR crossing requiring profile resolution. | Confirm the margin and flight-specific vertical profile. The map’s range is horizontal; the aircraft shows slant range. | Brief the full leg headings, assigned arc entry/exit, altitude reference, and recovery clearance. Check the reference values in the cockpit before issue. |
| Al Dhafra route conventions | Common-layer HI/LO routes include UNLTD-12000, 4000-8000, and 12000-4000 text. WEST ARC and SOUTH ARC are nominal 15 DME MA reconstructed from approximate linework. | Confirm altitude conventions, arc direction/exits, and recovery clearance. Check the named procedures in DCS before issue. |
